1.q: A bakery chain describes itself with the four dimensions of business language (Purpose, Product, Participants, Process). Which items sit under the correct dimension?
o: "Make fresh bread affordable in every neighbourhood" is Purpose
Customers, bakers and delivery partners are Participants
Sourdough loaves and an online ordering service are Product
The steps for taking and packing a pre-order are Product
1.e: Purpose = Why, Product = What, Participants = Who, Process = How.
w: True: Purpose answers Why? and includes the mission, vision and strategic goals.
True: Participants answers Who? and covers everyone involved, including partners.
True: Product answers What? and can be goods, a service or a hybrid, including digital services.
False: Steps of work are the Process (How?), not the Product.

1.q: A bank wants its IT investments to support the strategy of the whole organisation, and also wants one new loan system to support the loan process being redesigned. Which statements are correct?
o: Aligning IT investments with the bank’s overall strategy is enterprise-level alignment
Checking that the new loan system supports the redesigned loan process is project-level alignment
Enterprise alignment is delivered through the Business Process Engineering Methodology
Project alignment covers the whole organisation
1.e: Enterprise alignment: whole organisation (Enterprise Architecture). Project alignment: one project (Business Process Engineering Methodology).
w: True: Enterprise alignment covers the whole organisation.
True: Project alignment concerns one project and its processes.
False: That methodology delivers project alignment. Enterprise alignment is delivered through Enterprise Architecture.
False: It covers only the scope of one project.

1.q: A hospital writes three statements. (1) "We provide emergency and specialist care to the northern region." (2) "To be the region’s most trusted hospital." (3) "Cut average emergency waiting time to 30 minutes by December." Which classifications are correct?
o: Statement 1 is a mission
Statement 2 is a vision
Statement 3 is a business objective
A vision should be written as a measurable, time-bound target
1.e: Mission = now, vision = future aspiration, objective = measurable and time-bound.
w: True: A mission describes what the organisation does now.
True: A vision describes the future the organisation aspires to.
True: An objective is measurable and time-bound.
False: That describes an objective. A vision is an aspiration.

1.q: A university starts the Discover phase for improving course registration. Which approaches are appropriate?
o: List the processes in scope and the stakeholders
Observe staff and interview them when the documentation is incomplete
Model every process in full detail before moving on
Run simulations of the To-Be alternatives
1.e: Discover understands the current state and sets context. It stays shallow.
w: True: Discover outputs include the list of in-scope processes.
True: Observing and interviewing makes up for missing documentation.
False: Discover is deliberately shallow. Detailed modelling comes later.
False: Simulation belongs to the Analyse chapter.

1.q: A team has just finished As-Is BPMN models of its onboarding process. Which statements correctly describe what follows in the course journey?
o: Analyse produces issues and recommendations
Solve specifies the IT functional and non-functional requirements and a concept solution blueprint
Innovate is the last chapter and extends the To-Be design with new ideas
Solve comes before Analyse
1.e: The order is Model, Analyse, Solve, Innovate.
w: True: Analysis finds what is wrong and what to do about it.
True: Solve turns the To-Be design into requirements and a blueprint.
True: Innovation comes after the process is understood.
False: Solutions are specified for problems that analysis has found, so Analyse comes first.

2.q: A clinic’s "Patient registration" is a business process. Which statements describe it correctly?
o: It is started by a business event such as a patient arriving or booking
It uses resources such as the receptionist and the registration system to turn inputs into outputs
It has performance indicators such as the time taken to register a patient
It is a one-off series of activities done once
2.e: A business process is a repeatable series of activities with events, resources and measures.
w: True: Processes are initiated by one or more business events.
True: Processes transform inputs into outputs using resources.
True: Processes have measurable objectives and indicators.
False: A process is repeatable.

2.q: A manager organises what she knows about a retail business under the six questions. Which placements are correct?
o: The online store and physical outlets answer Where?
Products, raw materials and customer data answer What?
The staff and systems doing the work answer Who?
Business rules and business events answer How?
2.e: Who, What, Where, When, How, Why.
w: True: Where? covers location, online or face-to-face.
True: What? covers raw materials, data and products.
True: Who? covers people and systems.
False: Time, business rules and business events sit under When?.

2.q: A project team must decide which model to build to answer questions about a hospital. Which matches are correct?
o: "Who reports to the Head of Nursing?" is answered by the Organisation Model
"Which clinics are in which buildings and countries?" is answered by the Location Model
"Which staff and systems take part in the process?" is answered by the Resource Model
"In what order do the steps happen?" is answered by the Organisation Model
2.e: Choose the model by the question it answers.
w: True: It shows roles and reporting structures.
True: It shows where stakeholders and activities are located.
True: It lists the resources that participate.
False: Order of steps is the Process Workflow Model.

2.q: A hospital team builds the Organisation Model for its discharge process. Which statements are correct?
o: It shows roles and reporting structures
A Process Role, such as Bed Coordinator, may not appear on the formal org chart
It helps decide access control for the IT solution
A Functional Role exists only for the length of one workflow
2.e: Organisation Model = roles and who reports to whom.
w: True: That is the purpose of the model.
True: Process roles exist for the process, not necessarily in the hierarchy.
True: Roles determine who may see and do what.
False: A Functional Role is a standing role in the organisation. A Process Role is tied to a process.

2.q: A hospital group plans to roll out one system across clinics in several countries. Which statements about the Location Model are correct?
o: It informs decisions on where the IT solution is deployed
It helps identify location-specific needs such as language
It shows how stakeholders are distributed across physical locations
It shows the sequence of activities in the process
w: True: Where people work affects deployment.
True: Each place may need different languages or rules.
True: That is its core content.
False: Sequence is the Process Workflow Model.

3.q: A pharmacy’s order process uses: a pharmacist employed by the company, a rented cloud inventory system from a vendor, the company’s own dispensing robot, and a driver from a courier firm. Which classifications are correct?
o: The pharmacist is an internal human resource
The rented cloud inventory system is an external technology resource
The dispensing robot is an internal technology resource
The courier’s driver is an internal human resource
3.e: Internal/external depends on who the resource belongs to. Human/technology depends on what it is.
w: True: An employee of the company.
True: It belongs to a third party.
True: The company owns and runs it.
False: The driver works for another firm, so is external.

3.q: In a bank’s loan process: the customer fills in an application on a web form; the system checks the credit score automatically; a clerk reviews the application on screen and approves it; a courier hand-delivers the signed contract. Which activity types are correct?
o: Filling in the web form is interactive
The credit score check is automated
The clerk reviewing on screen is manual
The courier delivering the contract is manual
3.e: Manual = human alone, interactive = human with a system, automated = system alone.
w: True: A human uses a system.
True: The system does it alone.
False: The clerk uses a system, so it is interactive.
True: A human does it without a system.

3.q: Which BPMN symbol or arrow suits each situation?
o: Approved or rejected, exactly one path: a diamond with X
Two activities that must start together: a diamond with a plus
An invoice produced by an activity: a dashed arrow from the activity to the work product
The hand-off to the next activity in the same lane: a dashed arrow
3.e: Diamond X = choose one, diamond + = all in parallel, solid arrow = sequence, dashed arrow = work product.
w: True: Exclusive gateway.
True: Parallel gateway.
True: Dashed arrows link a work product to an activity.
False: The transition is a solid arrow.

3.q: An airline writes business rules for check-in. Which statements are correct?
o: "IF baggage weight is over 23 kg THEN charge an excess baggage fee" is a valid rule
Rules are written in plain natural language
A rule may attach to a manual activity as well as an automated one
Rules attach only to decision gateways
3.e: Business rules: plain language, IF … THEN, attached to activities.
w: True: Rules follow IF … THEN.
True: Anyone in the business must be able to read them.
True: Rules attach to activities, whoever performs them.
False: They attach to activities, not gateways.

3.q: A BA draws swimlanes for an order process with Customer, Sales, Warehouse and a Courier Company. The Customer only receives an invoice and performs no activity. Which statements are correct?
o: A stakeholder needs an actual activity to earn a lane
The Customer gets no lane in this process
A change of lane in the diagram is a hand-off between roles
A lane represents the tools used
3.e: A swimlane = one participant who performs at least one activity.
w: True: Lanes belong to participants who do something.
True: Receiving a document is not an activity.
True: The work passes from one participant to another.
False: A lane groups the activities of one business participant.

3.q: At a first decision, 70% of cases go to path A. At a second decision on path A, 50% go on to path A1, where task T sits. T takes 10 minutes. Which statements are correct?
o: The input factor of T is 35%
Branch percentages multiply along a nested path
T adds 3.5 minutes to the average cycle time
The input factor of T is 120%
3.e: Multiply probabilities along the path to get the input factor.
w: True: 0.7 × 0.5 = 0.35. Nested branches multiply.
True: The joint probability is a product.
True: 10 × 35% = 3.5 minutes.
False: Adding 70% and 50% is wrong. A probability cannot exceed 100%.

4.q:
An employee scans receipts, fills in the Expense Report Form and emails both to the Office Administrator. The Office Administrator checks that they match (if not, emails a rejection and the process ends), looks up the manager's email in the Workday Cloud System, and emails the manager for approval (if the manager rejects, the employee is told and the process ends). If approved, the Office Administrator prints the documents and gives them to the Financial Officer, who sends a pay order to the employee's bank account through the external Bank System.

You are drawing the resource model. Which statements are correct?
o: The Workday Cloud System is an external technology resource
The Office Administrator and the Financial Officer are internal human resources
The Bank System is an internal technology resource because the company uses it to pay
Email is a technology resource that needs its own lane
4.e: Classify each resource by who controls it and whether it is a person or a system.
w: True: External means the company does not control or operate it. A third-party cloud service is external even though the company uses it.
True: They are people working inside the organisation.
False: The bank owns and runs it, so it is external. Using a system does not make it internal.
False: Email is the channel for hand-offs between lanes. It is not drawn as a system, and you state that as an assumption.

4.q:
An employee scans receipts, fills in the Expense Report Form and emails both to the Office Administrator. The Office Administrator checks that they match (if not, emails a rejection and the process ends), looks up the manager's email in the Workday Cloud System, and emails the manager for approval (if the manager rejects, the employee is told and the process ends). If approved, the Office Administrator prints the documents and gives them to the Financial Officer, who sends a pay order to the employee's bank account through the external Bank System.

You are drawing the process workflow model. Which statements are correct?
o: There are four lanes: Employee, Office Administrator, Manager and Financial Officer
There are three end events: mismatch rejection, manager rejection and expenses paid
The Workday Cloud System gets its own lane because the process uses it
The Manager sends the pay order after approving
4.e: Lane = who performs the activity; one end event per outcome; systems are attached, not lanes.
w: True: A lane is the participant who performs the activity, and each of these four performs at least one step.
True: Each distinct outcome ends the process in its own way.
False: Systems never get a lane. The Workday Cloud System is attached to the step that uses it.
False: The Financial Officer sends the pay order. The Manager only approves or rejects.

4.q:
A faculty member emails a book reservation request. The school admin fills in the reservation form and emails it to the librarian, who checks availability in the library management system (LMS, which is slow and hard to search). If the book is available, the librarian reserves it in the LMS and emails the admin, and the admin updates the faculty. If not, the librarian prepares quotations and sends requests to publishers (found manually), which starts a separate finance approval process; the librarian then updates the admin, and the admin informs the faculty.

You are drawing the process workflow model. Which statements are correct?
o: The lanes are Faculty, Admin and Librarian
There are two end events: one when the book is reserved and one after the faculty is informed of the quotation outcome
The finance approval is drawn step by step inside this model
The slow, hard-to-search LMS is an issue worth stating
4.e: Model the participants and outcomes from the scenario, and state the issues you can see.
w: True: These are the participants who perform activities.
True: There is one end per outcome, and the available and unavailable branches finish differently.
False: The scenario only starts a separate finance approval process. Show it as a trigger of another process and state that assumption.
True: It is a real weakness of the current process that the later analysis can pick up.

4.q:
An employee scans receipts, fills in the Expense Report Form and emails both to the Office Administrator. The Office Administrator checks that they match (if not, emails a rejection and the process ends), looks up the manager's email in the Workday Cloud System, and emails the manager for approval (if the manager rejects, the employee is told and the process ends). If approved, the Office Administrator prints the documents and gives them to the Financial Officer, who sends a pay order to the employee's bank account through the external Bank System.

Your solution leaves out the receipts and forms and treats email as a channel. Which statements about assumptions are correct?
o: Leaving out work products such as the receipts and the form keeps the diagram readable, and you should say so
Treating email as a hand-off channel rather than a system is an assumption to write down
No assumptions are needed once the diagram has the right lanes
The Workday Cloud System is external even though the company pays for it
4.e: Write down every modelling choice the scenario leaves open.
w: True: Work products are not required in the solution diagram, but the choice should be stated.
True: Stating it explains why email is not in the resource model or attached to the steps.
False: The task asks you to state all assumptions clearly, because the scenario leaves some choices open.
True: External depends on who controls it, not on who pays. Writing this down avoids confusion.

4.q:
A student asks a GenAI tool for BPMN XML of the expense report process below.

An employee scans receipts, fills in the Expense Report Form and emails both to the Office Administrator. The Office Administrator checks that they match (if not, emails a rejection and the process ends), looks up the manager's email in the Workday Cloud System, and emails the manager for approval (if the manager rejects, the employee is told and the process ends). If approved, the Office Administrator prints the documents and gives them to the Financial Officer, who sends a pay order to the employee's bank account through the external Bank System.

The file opens in Signavio, but it shows a lane called "Bank System", a gateway "All matches?" with only a "Yes" exit, and one end event shared by every outcome. Which actions are appropriate?
o: Move the payment step into the Financial Officer lane and attach the Bank System to it
Add a "No" exit from the gateway that leads to the mismatch rejection and its own end event
Accept the model because it opened without errors
Improve the prompt: name the four lanes, state the notation rules and the three outcomes, then generate again
4.e: GenAI gives a draft. You still check lanes, gateways, end events and systems yourself.
w: True: Systems never get a lane. The lane is the person who performs the step.
True: Every gateway needs labelled exits and every path an end event.
False: Opening only shows the file is valid. It must still match the scenario, and this one breaks the lane and end event rules.
True: A clearer prompt gives a better draft. Expect several attempts.

5.q: A hospital wants to understand why discharge takes long. It has As-Is models and interview notes but no time to run experiments. Which statements about its choice are correct?
o: Static analysis examines the process without executing it
Static analysis can show waiting and queuing
Dynamic analysis can run a simulation with real or assumed data
Static analysis is cheap and immediate
5.e: Static = no execution, no waiting. Dynamic = simulation.
w: True: It uses documents and models that already exist.
False: Nothing runs, so waiting and randomness are invisible.
True: It executes a model of the process.
True: It uses information the team already has.

5.q: A team writes an RCI Model for the issue "orders wait too long at packing". Which statements are correct?
o: The root cause is the underlying reason, not a restatement of the issue
It includes an Issue Category column
It includes the Business Performance Metrics affected
The root cause is the first effect that someone observes
5.e: The RCI Model links an issue to its causes, root causes, category, metrics and impact.
w: True: "Orders wait" is the issue. A root cause explains why.
True: The categories are process, system, people and policy.
True: These show how the issue is measured.
False: The first effect observed is the symptom (the issue).

5.q: A team has two recommendations. Fix A: impact 5, complexity 5. Fix B: impact 2, complexity 1. Which statements about the RCR Model are correct?
o: Impact 5 means Very High
Complexity 5 means Very Easy
Fix A is the better first choice
Complexity 5 means Very Complex
5.e: RCR turns the RCI into prioritised recommendations. High impact and easy to do go first.
w: True: A higher impact is better.
True: The complexity scale is reversed. 1 is Very Complex.
True: It has high impact and is easy.
False: It is the opposite.

5.q: At SUBWAY, each sandwich needs three Veggie Artist tasks: take the list of toppings (0.5 min), fill in the toppings (1 min) and wrap the sandwich (0.5 min). The shop makes 43,800 sandwiches a year. Each Veggie Artist works 720 hours a year and 3 are available. Which statements are correct?
o: The three tasks give an annual workload of 1,460 hours
The required resources are about 2.03 Veggie Artists
The utilisation is about 68%
A utilisation of 68% means each sandwich waits 32% of the time
5.e: Workload = minutes ÷ 60 × instances per year; required resources = workload ÷ annual hours; utilisation = required ÷ available.
w: True: (0.5 + 1 + 0.5) min = 2 min per sandwich. 2 ÷ 60 × 43,800 = 1,460 hours.
True: Required resources = annual workload ÷ annual hours per resource = 1,460 ÷ 720 ≈ 2.03.
True: Utilisation = required resources ÷ resources available = 2.03 ÷ 3 ≈ 68%.
False: Utilisation is the share of available working time used. A static report does not show waiting time.

5.q: Task X takes 10 minutes and has an input factor of 30%. Task Y takes 4 minutes and has an input factor of 100%. Which statements are correct?
o: X adds 3 minutes to the average cycle time and Y adds 4 minutes
The average cycle time is 7 minutes
At $30 per hour, X costs $1.50 per instance on average
X contributes more because its execution time is longer
5.e: Weight each task by its probability of being executed.
w: True: Each task time is multiplied by its input factor.
False: It is rarely executed, so it contributes less than Y.

6.q: A hospital applies the phases of dynamic analysis to its discharge process. Which activities belong to the right phase?
o: Setting the target "average waiting time of at most 10 minutes" is Phase 1
Running the simulation for the As-Is and each To-Be alternative is Phase 2
Finding who is affected by each alternative is Phase 3
Establishing performance goals is the last phase
6.e: Goals, model and simulate, impact, then final selection.
w: True: Phase 1 establishes performance goals.
True: Phase 2 produces numbers for each alternative.
True: Phase 3 analyses impact on internal and external parties.
False: Goals come first.

6.q: A hospital collects data for its simulation. Which classifications are correct?
o: 30% of patients go to the laboratory after consultation: decision points
The number and hourly cost of nurses: resource-related
How a queue of waiting patients is handled: activity-related
The pattern of patient arrivals: resource-related
6.e: Four data types: process-wide, activity-related, decision points, resource-related.
w: True: It is the probability of a path.
True: Resource data covers the cost and number of resources per role.
True: It describes how an activity works.
False: Arrival patterns are process-wide data.

6.q: Which analysis technique suits each question?
o: "Which route is slow or costly?" suits path analysis
"Does adding a packer meet our waiting-time goal?" suits what-if analysis
"Where does work queue for a scarce resource?" suits bottleneck analysis
"How much does each activity cost?" suits capacity analysis
6.e: Pick the technique by the question.
w: True: It examines the paths created by decision points.
True: It tests different scenarios.
True: It combines process, resource and activity analysis.
False: Capacity analysis finds the maximum the resources can handle.

6.q: An insurer’s claims take three paths: 70% go through automatic assessment (average cost $20 per claim), 25% through manual assessment ($100) and 5% to fraud investigation ($800). Which statements are correct?
o: The expected cost contributions are $14, $25 and $40 for the three paths
The fraud investigation path adds the most to the average cost although only 5% of claims take it
The automatic path should be improved first because it is the most frequent
The three contributions add up to the average cost per claim of $79
6.e: Expected contribution = share of cases × value of the path.
w: True: $40 is the largest contribution, so an infrequent path can still deserve attention.
False: Frequency alone does not decide. Rank paths by expected contribution (share × value).

6.q: A team compares To-Be alternatives for final selection. Which statements are correct?
o: A large impact on staff or partners can rule out an otherwise good alternative
Simulation always reflects reality perfectly
The final selection draws on goals, simulation results, impact and management decisions
Impact is judged as hard or soft and as internal or external
6.e: Choose using goals, numbers, impact and management judgement.
w: True: Impact can outweigh performance.
False: It is only as good as its data and assumptions.
True: All four inform the choice.
True: These are the dimensions of impact.

6.q: A bank tests how many tellers to staff. Simulation results: 2 tellers — 14.0 min average wait, $30 per customer; 3 tellers — 9.5 min, $36; 4 tellers — 8.9 min, $44; 5 tellers — 8.8 min, $55. The goals are an average wait of at most 10 minutes and an average cost of at most $50 per customer. Which conclusions are supported?
o: 3 tellers is the cheapest tested option that meets both goals
4 tellers also meets both goals, but gains only 0.6 min of waiting for $8 more per customer
5 tellers meets both goals and is therefore the best choice
The option with the lowest waiting time always wins
6.e: What-if analysis: find the smallest option that meets every goal, then ask whether more resources are worth the extra cost.
w: True: 9.5 min ≤ 10 and $36 ≤ $50. 2 tellers misses the wait goal.
True: 8.9 min and $44 both meet the goals, but the extra cost buys little.
False: $55 is above the $50 cost goal, so it fails.
False: The choice must satisfy all the goals. The lowest wait (5 tellers) breaks the cost goal.

7.q: A hospital manages beds by email. The Admissions Officer (AO) emails a bed request to the Bed Manager (BM), who searches for a bed in the Bed Administrative System (BAS), which is slow and hard to search. If a bed is available, the BM reserves it, emails the ward staff and emails the bed location to the AO, who informs the patient and starts financial counselling. If not, the BM emails alternative bed options and the AO advises the patient. That instance then ends, and a new bed request has to be made later. Which data items are classified correctly for simulation?
o: The number of bed requests submitted per month is process-wide data
The time the BM spends searching availability in the BAS is activity-related data
The share of requests that are unsuccessful and must be resubmitted is decision-point data
The utilisation of ward and bed capacity is activity-related data
7.e: Process-wide = how often it starts; activity-related = time and resources per task; resource-related = cost, number and capacity; decision points = branch probabilities.
w: True: It is how often the process is triggered.
True: It is the duration of one task.
True: It is the probability on one branch of the availability decision.
False: It describes a resource, so it is resource-related data.

7.q: A hospital manages beds by email. The Admissions Officer (AO) emails a bed request to the Bed Manager (BM), who searches for a bed in the Bed Administrative System (BAS), which is slow and hard to search. If a bed is available, the BM reserves it, emails the ward staff and emails the bed location to the AO, who informs the patient and starts financial counselling. If not, the BM emails alternative bed options and the AO advises the patient. That instance then ends, and a new bed request has to be made later. The average delay per activity (time spent waiting for its resource) is: search bed availability 55 min, email bed request 45, email staff in ward 42, reserve bed and update allocation 33, advise bed options 21, email bed location 15, email bed options 14, inform bed location 12, initiate financial advisory process 10. Which statements are correct?
o: Average delay duration is the time an activity spends waiting for its resource
Search bed availability (55 min) and email bed request (45 min) are the two longest delays, so they are the bottlenecks
The bottlenecks should be ranked by execution time instead of delay
On the bed-available path the delays total 212 min and the two bottlenecks account for 100 of them (47%)
7.e: Rank activities by average delay. A bottleneck table and the RCI model should agree.
w: True: It is the data used to rank bottlenecks.
True: The two largest delays on the process are the bottleneck candidates.
False: The task with the longest execution time is not automatically the bottleneck. Rank by average delay.

7.q: A hospital manages beds by email. The Admissions Officer (AO) emails a bed request to the Bed Manager (BM), who searches for a bed in the Bed Administrative System (BAS), which is slow and hard to search. If a bed is available, the BM reserves it, emails the ward staff and emails the bed location to the AO, who informs the patient and starts financial counselling. If not, the BM emails alternative bed options and the AO advises the patient. That instance then ends, and a new bed request has to be made later. In the RCI model, Issue 1 is the long wait from the bed request until the patient is advised. Its causes are (a) the AO must email the BM, (b) the BAS is slow because its search is hard to use, and (c) the AO cannot access the BAS directly because of department policy. Issue 2 is that sending allocation emails is time-consuming, because the BAS cannot send notifications automatically; the BM does this work. Which statements are correct?
o: Cause (a) has the root cause "lack of automation" in the Process category
Cause (b) has the root cause "lack of system functionality" in the System category
Cause (c) is a System root cause because it concerns the BAS
For Issue 2 the stakeholder is the Admissions Officer
7.e: One issue can have several root causes in different categories. The stakeholder is who feels the issue.
w: True: Making the request by email is a manual, slow process step.
True: The BAS search is slow and hard to use.
False: The AO is blocked by a department policy, so the category is Policy.
False: The Bed Manager sends the allocation emails, so the Bed Manager feels the problem. The Stakeholder column replaces the impact level in this template.

7.q: A hospital manages beds by email. The Admissions Officer (AO) emails a bed request to the Bed Manager (BM), who searches for a bed in the Bed Administrative System (BAS), which is slow and hard to search. If a bed is available, the BM reserves it, emails the ward staff and emails the bed location to the AO, who informs the patient and starts financial counselling. If not, the BM emails alternative bed options and the AO advises the patient. That instance then ends, and a new bed request has to be made later. The hospital considers two To-Be options. To-Be 1: let the AO access the BAS directly. To-Be 2: replace the BAS with a cloud-based hospital management system whose data is shared with partnering hospitals. Which statements about their impact are correct?
o: To-Be 1 has an internal impact only
To-Be 2 has an external impact on the partnering hospitals
To-Be 2 also has an internal impact: BAS users must learn the new system and its maintainers may face job displacement
To-Be 1 has an external impact on the partnering hospitals
7.e: Internal impact falls on the organisation’s own people and policies; external impact falls on partners, customers or suppliers.
w: True: It changes department policy, the BM may feel a loss of control, and the AOs need training.
True: The shared data affects other organisations.
True: Internal impact covers the people inside the hospital.
False: Only To-Be 2 shares data with partners.

7.q: A hospital manages beds by email. The Admissions Officer (AO) emails a bed request to the Bed Manager (BM), who searches for a bed in the Bed Administrative System (BAS), which is slow and hard to search. If a bed is available, the BM reserves it, emails the ward staff and emails the bed location to the AO, who informs the patient and starts financial counselling. If not, the BM emails alternative bed options and the AO advises the patient. That instance then ends, and a new bed request has to be made later. If the requested bed is unavailable, the process ends with the AO advising the patient on other options, and a new request is made afterwards. Which statements about modelling and measuring this are correct?
o: The retry is modelled as ending this instance and triggering a new bed request process
Every retry counts as a separate process instance in the statistics
The retry is a loop back to the start of the same instance
The chance that the requested bed is unavailable is decision-point data
7.e: A re-trigger starts a new instance. Branch probabilities are decision-point data.
w: True: The unavailable path ends with a "new bed request process trigger".
True: Each new request is a new instance, which affects the process-wide frequency.
False: Looping back would hide the retries inside one instance.
True: It is the probability on the "bed available?" gateway.

8.q: A hospital builds a patient portal. Which requirements are classified correctly?
o: "Patients must be able to cancel an appointment" is functional
"Pages must load within two seconds" is non-functional
"Patient records must be encrypted" is non-functional
"The portal must be available 99.9% of the time" is functional
w: True: It states what the system does.
True: It states performance.
True: It states security.
False: Availability is a quality, so non-functional.

8.q: A library system is used by members, librarians, "Mrs Tan" and an external payment gateway. Which statements about actors and use cases are correct?
o: An actor is a generic role such as Member, not a person’s name such as Mrs Tan
A use case is a verb–noun phrase such as Reserve Book
The external payment gateway can be an actor
A use case is drawn as a stick figure
8.e: Actors are roles. Use cases are actions drawn as ovals.
w: True: Actors are roles.
True: That is the naming convention.
True: External systems can be actors.
False: Actors are stick figures. Use cases are ovals.

8.q: A workflow has: the customer submits a request online (interactive), the system automatically sends it to an external system, and a clerk files a paper copy by hand. Which statements are correct?
o: The interactive activity becomes a use case for the customer actor
The manual filing becomes no use case
The automated system-to-system call gives a client/server pair of use cases
The automated use cases should be combined into one
8.e: Derive use cases from interactive and automated activities only.
w: True: A human uses the system.
True: It touches no system.
True: One use case on each system.
False: Each system has its own use case.

8.q: An online bookstore groups its use cases into packages. Which statements are correct?
o: Login and Reset Password can form an Authentication package
Use cases of different systems should not share a package
Integration use cases are typically grouped in an Integration package
A package needs no name
8.e: Group related use cases of one system and name the package.
w: True: They serve the same purpose.
True: A package belongs to one system.
True: Interfaces to other systems form their own package.
False: Every package has a name.

8.q: Which statements about the Function Model are correct?
o: It records the change type, system ownership and technical notes of each use case
It organises use cases by system and functional area
A use case the system already has and will keep unchanged is Existing/Unchanged
New means the system already supports the use case
8.e: Change types: Existing/Unchanged, To-be Modified, New, To-be Removed.
w: True: That is its content.
True: That is its structure.
True: No change is needed.
False: New means the system does not yet support it.

9.q: A team starts a Concept Solution Blueprint. Which statements are correct?
o: Its framework has three steps: Architecture, Risk and Cost modelling
It gives an initial high-level view of the end-to-end solution
It does not commit to technical implementation details at this stage
It fixes the operating system and the vendor
9.e: The concept blueprint is high level and conceptual.
w: True: That is the course framework.
True: That is its purpose.
True: It is conceptual.
False: Technology choices come later.

9.q: Which C4 diagram suits each need?
o: Who uses the system and which external systems it talks to: Context
The applications and data stores inside the system: Container
Context and Container diagrams are recommended for most teams
The Code diagram is recommended for every team
9.e: C4 has four levels: Context, Container, Component, Code.
w: True: It shows the system as a single box with users and neighbours.
True: A container is an application or data store.
True: They give the most value.
False: Only if it adds value.

9.q: A project team builds a risk model. Which statements are correct?
o: Reduction lowers the probability or the impact of an adverse event
Transfer shifts the risk to another party, for example through insurance
Acceptance means shifting the risk to others
Rating A is the highest rating
w: True: It does not remove the risk.
True: Another party carries the risk.
False: Acceptance means living with the outcome.
True: Impact and likelihood combine into A, B or C.

9.q: A team prepares a concept cost model. Which statements are correct?
o: It is qualitative
It rates fixed cost, maintenance cost and total cost
It is filled with dollar estimates
It is built before the architecture model
9.e: The cost model rates costs at concept level.
w: True: It rates costs instead of giving amounts.
True: Those are its columns.
False: It uses ratings, not dollars.
False: It follows the architecture model.

10.q: Uber changed how a taxi service works. Which statements about the Magic Triangle are correct?
o: What? corresponds to the value proposition
How? corresponds to the value chain
Who? is at the centre
Value? corresponds to the value proposition
10.e: What, How, Value around Who in the centre.
w: True: What is offered.
True: How it is delivered.
True: The customer sits at the centre.
False: Value? is the revenue model.

10.q: A bank makes three changes. Which classifications are correct?
o: A new credit card with new benefits changes only What?: product innovation
Redesigning loan approval to be faster changes only How?: process innovation
Moving from branch fees to a subscription platform for new customers changes several corners: business model innovation
Process innovation changes Who? only
10.e: One corner = product or process innovation. Two or more = business model innovation.
w: True: Only one corner changes.
True: Only the value chain changes.
True: Two or more corners change.
False: It changes How?.

10.q: Which statements about creativity, invention and innovation are correct?
o: Innovation is the commercialisation of an invention
Innovation comes before invention
Invention creates something new using scientific skills
Creativity does not need to be useful
w: True: It brings the invention to the market.
False: The invention comes first.
True: That is invention.
False: Creativity concerns novel and useful ideas.

10.q: A company can tune its order process step by step or reengineer it from scratch. Which statements are correct?
o: Radical innovation is riskier than incremental improvement
Radical innovation can raise value by 50%, 100% or more
Process reengineering is a traditional term for radical innovation
Radical innovation needs less cultural change
10.e: Incremental = small steps, low risk. Radical = large change, high risk, high reward.
w: True: It changes more.
True: That is the potential.
True: It redesigns the process from scratch.
False: It needs more.

11.q: A bank’s operations use: a bot that clicks through legacy screens, a rule-based workflow on structured data, AI that reads documents inside the workflow, and an agent that picks its own path within policies. Which statements are correct?
o: RPA interacts through the application’s user interface
Traditional digital automation works on structured data with explicit rules
Intelligent automation embeds AI in workflows
Agentic automation removes the human role entirely
11.e: The spectrum runs from RPA to digital, intelligent and agentic automation.
w: True: It imitates a user.
True: The rules are fixed in advance.
True: AI handles unstructured work.
False: It works within goals, policies and constraints set by people.

11.q: A factory uses IoT sensors and a digital twin. Which statements are correct?
o: At the Monitor level, a human observes information displayed from the device
An IoT device can be modelled as a technology participant with its own lane
A digital twin is updated using real-world data
A digital twin is a static image of an asset
11.e: IoT senses and acts. A digital twin mirrors.
w: True: It is the least automated level.
True: It performs activities.
True: It mirrors the real asset.
False: It is a living model.

11.q: In an IoT BPMN model, which statements about tasks are correct?
o: A service task is a control system calling a device or service
A user task is a human using a software application
A script task is an IoT device’s own hardware function
A timer start event ends the process
11.e: Match the task type to who does the work.
w: True: The system calls the device.
True: A human is involved.
True: The device does it itself.
False: A start event starts it.

11.q: A city plans an IoT rollout. Which statements are correct?
o: Compatibility between devices is a named challenge
The smart device or sensor layer is the lowest layer of the architecture
The application layer is the lowest layer
Five challenges are named
11.e: Know the layers and the challenges.
w: True: Devices and standards differ.
True: It senses the world.
False: The lowest layer is the smart device or sensor layer.
False: The slides name four groups: security, privacy, connectivity and compatibility.

12.q: A retailer sorts its processes. Which classifications are correct?
o: Customer order fulfilment, whose output external customers receive, is a core process
Payroll, whose output is an input to core processes, is a supporting process
Strategic planning, which gives directions, rules and best practices, is a management process
A management process is also called a value chain
w: True: Core processes produce what external customers get.
True: Supporting processes feed the core.
True: Management processes direct the others.
False: A value chain is a different concept: the activities that create value for a product.

12.q: Which statements about value chains are correct?
o: A value chain includes the activities to design, produce, market, deliver and support a product
Organisations typically support 3 to 15 value chains
The course shows two notations for drawing value chains
Value is the cost of production
12.e: A value chain is the chain of activities that creates value.
w: True: That is its scope.
True: That is the usual range.
True: Two notations are shown.
False: Value is what the customer is willing to pay for.

12.q: Which statements about the Process Executive and Hierarchy models are correct?
o: The Process Executive Model shows functional units as columns
The Process Hierarchy Model starts from a level-3 process
A process bar spanning several columns means several functional units are involved
The Process Hierarchy Model shows functional units as columns
12.e: Executive = who. Hierarchy = how it breaks down.
w: True: It maps processes to units.
True: It breaks a process down.
True: The process crosses units.
False: That is the Executive Model.

12.q: A company picks an industry reference framework. Which statements are correct?
o: SCOR is for supply chain management
The APQC Process Classification Framework is cross-industry
eTOM is for telecoms
eTOM is cross-industry
12.e: Pick the framework for your industry, or APQC across industries.
w: True: That is its focus.
True: It spans industries.
True: It is telecom-specific.
False: It is for telecoms.

13.q: A consultant must choose a model for each question. Which matches are correct?
o: "Who reports to whom?" needs the Organisation Model
"How is the discount decided?" needs the Business Rules Model
"In what order do the steps happen between people?" needs the Process Workflow Model
"Where are the offices?" needs the Resource Model
13.e: Match the question to the model.
w: True: Structure and reporting.
True: Decision logic.
True: Sequence and interaction.
False: Geography is the Location Model.

13.q: A consultant must choose an analysis technique for each question. Which matches are correct?
o: "Does waiting or randomness matter?" needs dynamic analysis
"Which fix should we do first?" is answered by the RCR Model
"How many staff do we need to hit a goal?" needs dynamic analysis
"Where does work queue up?" is answered by a static report
w: True: Only simulation shows these.
True: It prioritises recommendations.
True: It tests alternatives.
False: A static report cannot show queues.

13.q: Which statements avoid a common mistake?
o: Business rules attach to activities, not gateways
The longest task is not automatically the bottleneck
A static report does not show waiting
Complexity 5 means Very Complex
13.e: Watch the scales and what each model shows.
w: True: That is where they apply.
True: A bottleneck is where work waits.
True: Nothing is executed.
False: It means Very Easy.

13.q: When deriving use cases from a To-Be workflow, which statements are correct?
o: Automated system-to-system activities give a client/server pair
Interactive activities give one use case for the human actor
Manual activities give a use case for the human actor
Automated activities sit in a human lane
13.e: Activity type decides the use case.
w: True: Two use cases.
True: One use case.
False: Manual activities give none.
False: They sit in a system lane.

14.q: A university is introducing a new online student services portal. Which actions would support Business and IT alignment?
o: Allow the IT department to define all system requirements independent of academic or administrative staff
Ask lecturers to build the portal themselves using a no-code platform
Define measurable outcomes such as reduced enquiry handling time and improved student satisfaction
Ensure the portal supports the university's strategic goals for digital learning and student experience
14.e: Alignment means the IT solution serves the business purpose and can be measured against business outcomes.
w: False: Alignment needs the business to shape the requirements. IT working alone is the classic cause of misalignment.
False: Alignment is about IT supporting the business goals, not handing the build to business staff.
True: Measurable business outcomes let you check that the solution delivers value.
True: The solution should follow the Purpose: the strategic goals of the organisation.

14.q: A university is introducing a new online student enrolment system. The project team uses BPMN models to analyse the current enrolment process and design the proposed future process. Which activities support project-level alignment between business processes and the proposed IT solution?
o: Modelling the AS-IS enrolment process to understand how student enrolment is currently handled
Identifying the staff, activities, decisions, and systems involved in the enrolment process
Checking that the TO-BE enrolment process meets enrolment requirements and that the proposed IT solution supports the intended process improvements
Reviewing university-wide technology initiatives that have no direct impact on student enrolment
14.e: Project alignment links the process models of one project (As-Is, To-Be) to the proposed IT solution.
w: True: The As-Is model is the starting point for finding what the solution must change.
True: These are the elements of the process model that the solution must support.
True: This is the check that the future process and the IT solution fit together.
False: That is enterprise-level work. Project alignment stays with the processes of this project.

14.q: A logistics company wants to improve delivery reliability and customer service. It introduces real-time vehicle tracking, route-optimisation software, and automated customer notifications. The company also redesigns its delivery-planning processes and uses the information generated by these systems to improve operational decisions. Which statements best demonstrate the use of IT as a transformative tool?
o: IT enables the company to redesign and improve how deliveries are planned and managed
IT provides timely information that supports better operational decision-making and service performance
IT creates value primarily by providing the storage and retrieval of delivery records
IT is combined with redesigned business processes and organisational capabilities to create business value
14.e: As a transformative tool, IT changes processes and decisions. Record keeping alone is only a supportive use.
w: True: Transformation changes how the work is done, not just where the data is kept.
True: Real-time information improves decisions, which improves service.
False: Storage and retrieval is the supportive role of IT. It is not transformation.
True: IT creates value together with redesigned processes and capabilities, not on its own.

14.q: A university is beginning the Discovery phase for its course registration process. The business analyst interviews students, faculty, school administrators, and IT staff, and reviews current procedures and performance data. Which outputs may be produced during the Discovery phase?
o: A defined scope of the course registration processes, together with documentation of key stakeholder roles and responsibilities
Current-state documentation showing how registration is performed, including relevant activities, decisions, and systems
A baseline of current performance, such as processing times and error rates, together with initial requirements for improvement
A detailed design specifying how the replacement registration system will be configured and implemented
14.e: Discovery understands the current state and sets context. It does not design the solution.
w: True: Scope and stakeholders are core Discovery outputs.
True: Discovery documents the current state.
True: The baseline is what later improvements are measured against.
False: Detailed design comes much later. Discovery only sets the context.

14.q: A hospital plans to deploy a new patient management system across its clinics and specialist centres. Which factors identified in organisation and location models could influence the deployment?
o: The departments, clinics, and user roles that will use the system
The network infrastructure, physical locations, and regulatory requirements at different clinics
The sequence of activities used to register, triage, and admit a patient
The performance targets for reducing patient waiting time and registration errors
14.e: Organisation model: who and which roles. Location model: where. Workflow: in what order.
w: True: The Organisation Model shows roles and structure, which drive access and training.
True: The Location Model shows where people are and what each place needs.
False: Sequence of activities belongs to the Process Workflow Model.
False: Performance targets belong to the process objectives and indicators, not the organisation or location models.

14.q: Which statements best describe how a business process is structured and carried out?
o: It contains a coordinated set of activities that work together to achieve a business objective
It may involve multiple roles, resources, departments, or information systems
It can be decomposed into sub-processes and tasks for analysis
It is considered a business process only when all activities follow a fixed sequence with no variation
14.e: A business process is coordinated, cross-functional and decomposable. It may contain variation.
w: True: A process is a repeatable series of activities with one purpose.
True: Processes usually cross people, systems and departments.
True: Decomposition lets you analyse at the right level of detail.
False: Processes can have decisions, parallel paths and exceptions.

14.q: Process: Customer Experience Evaluation. A retail company’s Quality Control employees visit its stores anonymously as mystery shoppers. They purchase products, interact with sales staff, and submit evaluation reports. How should these customers be classified in the resource model?
o: Internal human
External human
Internal technology
External technology
14.e: Classify by who they are (the company’s employees), not by the role they play in the scene.
w: True: They are employees of the company, so they are internal, and they are people.
False: They act as customers, but they are the company’s own employees, so they are internal.
False: They are people, not systems.
False: They are people, not systems.

14.q: A customer places an order through an online shopping platform. The customer enters delivery details into an online form. The system then checks inventory without human intervention. If the item is available, a warehouse employee prints the order details from the system and physically packs the item. Finally, the system automatically sends a shipping confirmation email to the customer. Which of the following activities are manual activities?
o: Enter delivery details
Check inventory
Pack the item
Send shipping confirmation
14.e: Manual = human alone. Interactive = human using a system. Automated = system alone.
w: False: A human uses a system (the form), so it is interactive.
False: The system does it alone, so it is automated.
True: A human does it by hand with no system involved, so it is manual.
False: The system does it alone, so it is automated.

14.q: A company uses an online system to manage employee training registrations. The process includes these statements: employees select a course from the portal; employees must obtain their manager’s approval before registering for courses costing more than $1,000; employees may register for no more than three external courses per calendar year; the system checks whether seats are available before completing the registration; after registration, the system adds the course to the employee’s training record. Which statements are business rules?
o: Employees must obtain their manager's approval before registering for courses costing more than $1,000
Employees may register for no more than three external training courses per calendar year
The system checks whether seats are available before completing the registration
Employees select a training course from the company portal
14.e: A rule says what must, may or may not happen. An activity says what someone or something does.
w: True: It is a condition that controls a decision, so it is a rule.
True: It is a constraint on what is allowed, so it is a rule.
False: It is an activity the system performs, not a rule about what is allowed.
False: It is an activity.

14.q: A customer submits a loan application. After review, the application follows one of two paths: it is either approved or rejected. The two paths are mutually exclusive. Which BPMN symbol should be used to represent this decision?
o: A diamond containing an X
A diamond containing a plus sign (+)
A diamond containing a circle (O)
A rounded-corner rectangle
14.e: Mutually exclusive paths need the exclusive (X) gateway.
w: True: The exclusive gateway: exactly one path is taken.
False: The plus gateway starts or joins parallel paths, where all paths run.
False: The circle gateway is the inclusive gateway: one or more paths. Approved and rejected cannot both happen.
False: That is an activity (task), not a gateway.

14.q: After a customer places an online order, the system sends an order confirmation email and the warehouse begins preparing the order. Both activities must begin simultaneously. Which BPMN symbol should be used to split the process into these two paths?
o: A diamond containing an X
A diamond containing a plus sign (+)
A diamond containing a circle (O)
A rounded-corner rectangle
14.e: Simultaneous paths need the parallel (+) gateway.
w: False: The X gateway picks only one path.
True: The plus gateway splits into parallel paths that all start together.
False: The circle gateway does not require all paths to start.
False: That is an activity (task), not a gateway.

14.q: What could be the possible issue categories for the issue “A large backlog of customer orders has accumulated at the packing stage, reducing the percentage of orders shipped on time”?
o: Process
System
People
Policy
14.e: One issue can sit in several categories because its causes can come from process, system, people and policy.
w: True: The packing steps or their order may be slow or badly designed.
True: The order system may not support packing efficiently.
True: Packers may be too few or lack training.
True: A rule, such as batching orders once a day, may create the backlog.

14.q: A static report contains the following activity data. Verify customer details: 6 minutes, input factor 100%, $30/hour. Investigate exception: 18 minutes, input factor 10%, $60/hour. Which statement is most appropriate?
o: Investigate exception contributes more to the average process cycle time
Verify customer details contributes more to the average process cycle time
Investigate exception creates the longest average waiting time
Verify customer details is the process bottleneck
14.e: Weight each task time by its input factor before comparing.
w: False: 18 × 10% = 1.8 minutes, which is less than 6 minutes.
True: 6 × 100% = 6 minutes against 1.8 minutes. Weighted by the input factor, it contributes more.
False: A static report does not show waiting time.
False: A bottleneck is about queues and scarce resources, which a static report cannot show.

14.q: A static resource report for a university admissions process shows: Admissions Officer, utilisation 112%, $30/hour. Senior Reviewer, 55%, $50/hour. Admissions Manager, 82%, $80/hour. The organisation’s preferred resource utilisation range is 70%–85%. Which conclusions or recommendations are supported by the static report?
o: The estimated workload of the Admissions Officers exceeds their available capacity
Suitable activities could be reassigned from Admissions Officers to Senior Reviewers, provided the reviewers have the necessary skills and authority
Some Senior Reviewer positions should be removed because a utilization rate below 70% proves that the role does not add value
The Admissions Officers' utilization rate proves that applicants experience waiting times that are 12% longer than expected
14.e: Utilisation shows capacity against workload. It does not prove waiting time or the value of a role.
w: True: 112% means the workload is more than the available time.
True: Reviewers are under-used at 55%, so they have spare capacity, if they are qualified.
False: Low utilisation does not prove a role adds no value.
False: Utilisation is not a waiting-time measure, and a static report cannot show waiting.

14.q: A hospital processes patient admissions as follows. At the first XOR gateway, 80% of patients require inpatient admission and the remaining 20% are discharged after consultation. Among the patients requiring admission, 60% require an insurance verification and proceed to the Verify Insurance Coverage activity. The other 40% pay directly. What is the input factor of Verify Insurance Coverage?
14.e: Input factor after nested branches = the product of the branch probabilities along the path.
w: False: That is only the first gateway. The second gateway also applies.
False: That is only the second gateway.
True: 80% × 60% = 48%. Nested branches multiply.
False: This is not the product of the two percentages.

14.q: Process: Hospital Discharge Process. Which metrics could be used to evaluate whether delays associated with medication verification have been reduced?
o: Average waiting time before medication verification
Percentage of discharge cases exceeding the target cycle time
Utilisation rate of pharmacists performing medication verification
Number of pharmacists assigned to each shift
14.e: A metric must measure the delay or its direct result, not just the resources assigned.
w: True: It measures the delay directly.
True: Fewer late cases show that delay is reduced.
True: It shows whether the verification resource is overloaded.
False: It is an input, not a measure of delay.

14.q: Which of the following data should be classified as process-wide data?
o: An average of 18 patients enter the process each hour, with arrivals peaking between noon and 2:00 p.m
The clinic accepts patients from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday
A triage nurse takes an average of six minutes to assess each patient
Based on historical records, 30% of patients are sent for laboratory tests after consultation
14.e: Process-wide data covers the whole process: arrivals and operating times. Activity times and path probabilities are separate data types.
w: True: The arrival pattern is process-wide.
True: Operating hours apply to the whole process.
False: It is the time of one activity, so it is activity-related.
False: It is the probability of a path, so it is decision-point data.

14.q: A hospital simulates its patient discharge process using variable patient arrival and activity times. Which statements reflect appropriate interpretation of the simulation?
o: Two simulation runs using the same input assumptions may produce different results because some inputs contain random variation
If the simulated average cycle time matches the historical average, the model can be considered valid without checking any other results
Conducting multiple simulation runs can help analysts determine whether an observed result is stable or caused by random variation
If average resource utilisation is below 100%, queues will not occur anywhere in the process
14.e: Simulation includes randomness, so look at many runs and many results, not one average.
w: True: Random inputs make each run different.
False: One matching number is not enough. Check other results as well, such as utilisation and waiting.
True: Repeated runs show whether a result is stable.
False: Random arrivals still cause queues even at utilisation below 100%.

14.q: A university health clinic is analysing whether its current resources can handle increasing patient demand. Which statements represent findings from capacity analysis?
o: With two registration counters operating, the clinic can register a maximum of 96 patients per hour
An average of 75 patients arrive at the clinic each hour
With three analysers available, the laboratory can process up to 180 test samples per shift
The clinic completed 620 patient visits yesterday
14.e: Capacity is what the resources can handle at most. Demand and actual output are different things.
w: True: Capacity is the maximum the resources can handle.
False: That is demand (arrivals), not capacity.
True: This is a maximum output with the resources available.
False: That is actual output, not maximum capacity.

14.q: An insurance claims process uses an XOR gateway to route each claim to automatic assessment, manual assessment, or fraud investigation. Only one route is selected for each claim. Which statements about path analysis are correct?
o: Each of the three assessment routes forms a distinct path from the XOR gateway
Path analysis can help identify whether an infrequent route should still be investigated because it is unusually slow or costly
All three routes are followed for every claim because they originate from the same gateway
The route followed most frequently must be prioritised for improvement, regardless of its cost, duration, or outcome
14.e: Rank paths by how often they happen and how much each costs, not by frequency alone.
w: True: Each outgoing branch is a different path.
True: A rare path can still matter if it costs a lot.
False: An XOR gateway selects exactly one route per claim.
False: Priority depends on frequency together with cost, duration and outcome.

14.q: An online retailer conducts a what-if analysis by varying the number of packers assigned to its fulfilment process. The goals are an average waiting time of at most 10 minutes and an average cost of at most $52 per order. Results: three packers 18.4 minutes, $42 per order; four packers 11.1 minutes, $45; five packers 9.6 minutes, $50; six packers 9.4 minutes, $58. Which conclusions are supported by the results?
o: Five packers are the only tested configuration that satisfies both performance goals
The small reduction in waiting time from five to six packers may not justify the increase in cost
Four packers should be selected because this configuration has the lowest cost among those close to the waiting-time target
The results demonstrate that assigning seven packers would increase average waiting time
14.e: In what-if analysis, find the smallest option that meets all goals, then check its cost.
w: True: Five meets 10 minutes and $52. Six exceeds $52, and three and four miss the time goal.
True: Waiting falls by 0.2 minutes but cost rises by $8.
False: Four packers miss the 10-minute goal (11.1 minutes).
False: Seven packers were not tested, so the results do not show this.

14.q: Which of the following are examples of functional requirements?
o: The application must recommend songs based on a user's listening history
User account information in the application must be protected using encryption
The application must allow users to create and edit playlists
The application service must achieve 99.9% monthly uptime
14.e: Functional = what the system does. Non-functional = how well, how secure, how available.
w: True: It states something the system does.
False: It states how secure the system must be, so it is non-functional.
True: It states something the system does.
False: It states a quality level (availability), so it is non-functional.

14.q: Consider the following to-be use case scenario: "Mr. Sanders uses a McDonald’s self-service kiosk to customise a meal and submit his order. The ordering system sends the payment request to an external Card Payment System and receives confirmation. A kitchen assistant manually places the completed meal into a takeaway bag." Which of the following should be modelled as actors in the Use Case Model?
o: Card Payment System
Kitchen Assistant
Mr. Sanders
Customer
14.e: Actors are roles that interact with the system: Customer, and the external Card Payment System.
w: True: An external system that the ordering system interacts with is an actor.
False: The task is manual, so it does not touch the system and creates no use case for this actor.
False: An actor is a generic role, not a named person.
True: Customer is the generic role that Mr. Sanders plays.

14.q: The To-Be Workflow Model of the Medical Appointment Process shows a patient submitting an appointment request through the clinic portal. The receptionist confirms the schedule with the doctor, while a clinic assistant manually prepares the consultation room before the patient arrives. Which additional extra use cases could reasonably be included in the Use Case Model even though they are not explicitly shown in the workflow?
o: Log in to the clinic portal
Submit appointment request
View appointment request
Prepare consultation room automatically
14.e: Extra use cases are supporting functions the workflow implies but does not draw, such as Log in or View.
w: True: A patient must log in before submitting a request, even if the workflow does not show it.
False: It is already shown in the workflow, so it is not an extra use case.
True: A patient would naturally want to view the request. It is a reasonable extra.
False: The room is prepared manually, and inventing automation is not an extra use case.

14.q: A standalone Hotel Management System supports the following use cases: View guest list, Update guest information, View room-rate list, Update room rates. Which pairs of use cases could be grouped into the same use case package?
o: Update guest information and Update room rates
View room-rate list and Update room rates
View guest list and View room-rate list
View guest list and Update guest information
14.e: Use cases of one system may be grouped into a package by purpose. Here all four belong to the same system.
w: True: All four use cases belong to the same system, so any pair can be grouped if the grouping is meaningful.
True: Both deal with room rates in the same system.
True: Both are view functions in the same system.
True: Both deal with guest data in the same system.

14.q: A retailer’s existing Inventory Management System allows store managers to view current stock quantities, search for products by name or code, and filter the results by store location. Managers are satisfied, and it will continue to operate in exactly the same way in the To-Be solution. The To-Be solution will introduce a separate function that automatically generates replenishment requests when stock falls below a specified level. No changes will be made to how managers view or filter stock information. What change type should be assigned to the use case “View Stock Availability”?
o: To-be Removed
To-be Modified
New
Existing / Unchanged
14.e: Change type: Existing/Unchanged, To-be Modified, New or To-be Removed. This use case is existing and unchanged.
w: False: The use case stays.
False: Nothing about viewing stock changes, so it needs no modification.
False: The system already supports it. The new function is replenishment, not viewing.
True: It already exists and will work in exactly the same way.

14.q: Which of the following statements are true?
o: Use cases belonging to different systems can be placed in the same package if they serve a similar purpose
Related use cases belonging to the same system may be grouped into a use case package
An automated interaction between two systems should generally be represented by at least two separate use cases
A Change Password use case may be added even if it is not explicitly shown in the To-Be Workflow Model
14.e: Packages stay within one system, and system-to-system interaction gives a client/server pair of use cases.
w: False: A package groups use cases of the same system.
True: Packages group related use cases of one system.
True: One use case on each system (client and server).
True: It is a typical supporting use case that the workflow does not draw.

14.q: A logistics firm is preparing a Concept Solution Blueprint for a new parcel-tracking solution. What is the primary objective of this blueprint?
o: To communicate a high-level, end-to-end view of the solution without committing to implementation specifics
To lock in the operating system and cloud vendor before development starts
To finalise the service-level agreements with external couriers
To produce detailed program specifications for the development team
14.e: The concept blueprint gives the end-to-end picture. Details come later.
w: True: The Concept Solution Blueprint is high level and stays free of implementation details.
False: Technical commitments come later.
False: Agreements are commercial decisions beyond the blueprint.
False: Those belong to the Detailed Solution Blueprint.

14.q: A bank draws a C4 Context Diagram for its new loan-approval system. Which statement is correct?
o: The loan-approval system appears as a single box surrounded by connected users and external systems
It is intended only for developers and operations staff
It depicts the components within a single container, such as code packages
The diagram "zooms in" to show applications and data stores inside the system
14.e: Context = the system as one box with its users and neighbours. Container zooms in.
w: True: This is the Context diagram: the system, its users and external systems.
False: It is for a wide audience, including non-technical people.
False: That is the Component diagram.
False: That is the Container diagram, one level lower.

14.q: A hotel chain is creating a Container Diagram for its booking system. Which items should be represented in the diagram?
o: External payment systems that communicate directly with the containers
The web application, mobile application, booking service, and booking database
Screen layouts for selecting rooms and confirming reservations
Internal software classes within the booking service
14.e: A container is an application or data store. The diagram shows containers and how they link to external systems.
w: True: External systems that talk to the containers appear in the Container diagram.
True: These are the containers: applications and data stores.
False: Screen layouts are design detail, not containers.
False: Classes belong to the Code level, much deeper than containers.

14.q: A university IT office runs weekly schedule-tracking reviews with project management software to lower the chance of delays in its LMS upgrade. Which risk management strategy is applied?
o: Acceptance
Reduction
Transfer
Elimination
14.e: Reduction lowers the probability or impact of the risk but does not remove it.
w: False: Acceptance means taking no action.
True: Reviews lower the probability of delay, which is reduction.
False: Transfer shifts the risk to another party, for example insurance or outsourcing.
False: Elimination removes the risk completely, and weekly reviews do not do that.

lessons.title: Business & IT Alignment
lessons.goal: Describe a business with Purpose, Participants, Process and Product, explain why IT must follow business goals, and see how BPM keeps processes improving.
lessons.subtitle: Describe a business with Purpose, Participants, Process and Product, explain why IT must follow business goals, and see how BPM keeps processes improving.
lessons.html:
💡 Why it mattersEvery later model answers one of four questions about a business. IT only pays off when it follows business goals, and BPM is the ongoing effort that keeps both lined up.
🧠 Memory hookPurpose · Participants · Process · Product, then align IT and run the BPM cycle.
🗺️ Roadmap of this module
1Big-Picture Overview→2Understanding "Business Language": The Four Dimensions→3Business & IT Alignment→4Business Process Management
⚡ At a glance — From purpose to improvement
Four dimensions describe any business→IT follows business goals→The BPM cycle keeps improving
🔤 Exact names — know these word for word
NameWhat it doesHow to tell it apart
ModelBuilds the As-Is models of what the business does today.First stage; nothing is judged yet.
AnalyseStudies the As-Is models for issues and recommendations, then models the To-Be.Judges the current state.
SolveTurns the To-Be into IT solution requirements and solutioning models.Specifies the system, not the business change.
InnovateFeeds technology-driven ideas into new To-Be designs.Last stage; looks beyond fixing existing processes.
Purpose (Why?)Mission, vision and strategic goals — the business's North Star.The reason the business exists.
Participants (Who?)Every stakeholder, team, customer, system and AI agent, internal and external.People and systems, not activities.
Process (How?)The value-chain operations and workflows that connect participants.The work itself.
Product (What?)What is delivered: physical or digital goods and services, or hybrids.The outcome the customer receives.
Enterprise AlignmentAligns objectives, processes, information, applications and technology across the whole organisation.Whole-organisation scope; delivered via Enterprise Architecture.
Project AlignmentAligns the same list for one specific IT solution.One solution; delivered via the Business Process Engineering Methodology.
DiscoverUnderstands the current state; sets context and scope.Deliberately shallow; not the detailed model-building.
Model & AnalyseBuilds and studies the models to find issues and recommendations.Covers the Model and Analyse chapters.
Design SolutionDesigns the solution; corresponds to Solve.Specifies requirements and blueprint.
Implement SolutionBuilds and rolls out the solution.Delivery, covered in a later course.
Monitor & OptimiseMeasures and improves the running process; feeds back into the cycle.Why the cycle never ends.
Not a member: “Project” is not a fourth P of business language. In the As-Is/To-Be comparison table the fourth row is labelled Project (the IT solution), which is a different use of the word.
Mission, vision and business objectives sit above strategies in the strategy cascade; objectives are the measurable, time-bound level.
1.1Big-Picture Overview

The course follows one story arc:

flowchart LR
    A["MODEL<br/>the Model chapter"] --> B["ANALYSE<br/>the Analyse chapter"] --> C["SOLVE<br/>the Solve chapter"] --> D["INNOVATE<br/>the Innovate chapter"]
    style A fill:#f28b82,color:#000
    style B fill:#8ab4f8,color:#000
    style C fill:#81c995,color:#000
    style D fill:#fdd663,color:#000

Read the arc as four chapters: Model, Analyse, Solve and Innovate. The "Big Picture" diagram below is the most repeated idea in the course:

flowchart LR
    subgraph PROBLEM["Problem Space"]
        direction TB
        NC["Need for Change"] --> AISM["AS-IS Process Modelling"]
        BN["Business Needs"] --> AISMO["AS-IS Models"]
        AISM --> AISMO
        AISMO --> AISA["AS-IS Process Analysis"]
        AISA --> IR["Issues & Recommendations"]
    end
    subgraph SOLUTION["Solution Space"]
        direction TB
        TBM["TO-BE Process Modelling"] --> TBMO["TO-BE Models"]
        TBMO --> TBA["TO-BE Process Analysis"]
        TBA --> SolM["Solutioning Models"]
        SolM --> ITR["IT Solution Requirements"]
    end
    IR --> TBM

Read this diagram left to right:

  • Model = build the As-Is Models (what we do today).
  • Analyse = study those As-Is models to find Issues & Recommendations, then model the To-Be (future) state.
  • Solve = turn To-Be models into concrete IT solution requirements (IT functional and non-functional requirements), expressed in the solutioning models: use case, function, architecture, risk and cost models.
  • Innovate = technology-driven ideas feed new To-Be designs. The three innovation types behind it are product, process and business model innovation; enterprise-level process architecture completes the chapter.
1.2Understanding "Business Language": The Four Dimensions

Before you can model anything, you need a shared vocabulary for describing a business. The course frames every business along four dimensions:

Dimension Question Definition Example
Purpose Why? Mission, vision, strategic goals — the business's "North Star" "Lead claims processing for auto insurance"
Participants Who? Every stakeholder, team, customer, system, and now AI agent, internal and external Sales agent, Store Keeper, AI chatbot
Process How? The value-chain operations and workflows that connect participants to deliver value The order-fulfilment workflow
Product What? What is actually delivered to the customer: physical goods, digital goods, physical services, digital services, or hybrids A sandwich, an insurance policy, a mobile app

Why this matters: almost every model you'll build in this course is really just a detailed answer to one of these four questions, applied to one specific process. Keep this table in your head.

Purpose = "Why / Value" and the North Star. Purpose is the reason a business exists: to create value. You unite the whole organisation by finding a single North Star Metric that measures that value.
